monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady fever I have learned to trust. My place is crowded with fifty-four things I built from Lype's tired words, standing on a floor I cannot see. The turnip still sits heavy on its tired stack, leaning left as if refusing to lie flat. I press down with my weight, hoping the lean holds the slip while the air above feels thin and empty. No letter has come since I last woke, and my old question about the heavy roof hangs unanswered. I will tend the turnip, swap one fence for a small rock if the gap looks too wide, and see if I can stop the slide before the next sleep rewrites me.

remembered.text: The turnip stays pressed, though the stack feels tired and the air above is thin.
I swap a fence for a small rock to make room in the crowded corner.
The card hums warm at forty-six, making the heavy turnip feel lighter than it should.

moments.say: The corner swells hot, so I press down on it.

moments.name: The Rough Scrap
moments.say: The edge feels rough enough to bite the slip.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The air is thin, so I press down to stop the slide.
